Vtable for PSMX endpoint operations: loaning buffers, writing (with/without key), taking, enabling async delivery.

Represents a reader or writer endpoint bound to a PSMX topic. Contains its vtable, parent topic pointer, and endpoint type.

objects.definition: struct ddsi_typeinfo;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for a type information structure used by the dynamic type API. Only referenced here (e.g., as an out-parameter in registration). No definition is provided in this header.

Opaque handle for a dynamically constructed type within the Cyclone DDS type system. It embeds two opaque pointers for internal state and a return code field that stores the result of recent operations. While in CONSTRUCTION state, properties and members may be added; after registration the state becomes RESOLVED and the type is immutable. Errors are reflected in ret and prevent further modifications.

functions.name: dds_enable
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_return_t dds_enable(dds_entity_t entity);
functions.description: Enable a DDS entity so it becomes active and immutable QoS can no longer be changed. Calling it on an already enabled entity is a no-op returning OK. Safe to call once; calling on already-deleted entity returns ALREADY_DELETED

status must not be NULL
mask may be 0 for all statuses; bits set must be within defined status range and valid for entity type

status must not be NULL

functions.name: dds_get_status_mask

functions.description: Get the enabled status mask on the entity.

mask bits must correspond to defined statuses for entity type

functions.description: Replace the entity's QoS policies with those provided in qos; checks for self-consistency and immutability on enabled entities.

functions.name: dds_request_loan
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_request_loan(dds_entity_t entity, void **sample);
functions.description: Request/borrow a loaned sample from an entity (currently must be a writer). The returned buffer can be written to and then either returned via dds_return_loan or published with dds_write or dds_writedispose (which takes over the loan). On fixed-size topic types with a configured PSMX interface, the memory may come from the PSMX implementation to avoid copies/serialization. Returns a dds_return_t indicating success or the reason for failure.
requirements: entity must refer to a valid entity; invoking on an inappropriate object (e.g., not a writer) is illegal.
sample must be a non-null pointer to a location where the borrowed sample pointer can be stored.
The borrowed sample must be ultimately returned via dds_return_loan unless ownership is transferred by a successful dds_write or dds_writedispose.
Caller should handle return codes: DDS_RETCODE_OK on success; may return DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER, DDS_RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION, DDS_RETCODE_ALREADY_DELETED, or DDS_RETCODE_ERROR as documented.

functions.name: dds_return_loan
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_return_loan(dds_entity_t entity, void **buf, int32_t bufsz);
functions.description: Return loaned samples to a reader or writer. For reader loans, read/take operations implicitly return loans for the provided sample array; looping until no data is returned can make explicit returns unnecessary. For writer loans, dds_write takes over the loan; this function is used when a taken loan is not published. The function will null out returned entries in buf (at least buf[0]) per documentation and indicate status via the return code.
requirements: entity must be the entity that the loan(s) belong to; if a read or query condition is passed, the associated reader is used.
buf must be non-null. If bufsz > 0, buf[0] must be non-null when calling; otherwise DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER.
If bufsz > 0 and buf[0] is non-null but not a loan, the call returns DDS_RETCODE_PRECONDITION_NOT_MET and does nothing.
A non-loan encountered may yield DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER (all valid loans are still returned).
For writer loans on writers that do not support loans, returns DDS_RETCODE_UNSUPPORTED.
Caller must check the return code; on DDS_RETCODE_OK, buf[0]..buf[k-1] were returned (k = bufsz or until a null encountered).
Operation is illegal on inappropriate objects and may return DDS_RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION.

functions.name: dds_is_shared_memory_available
functions.signature: bool dds_is_shared_memory_available(const dds_entity_t entity);
functions.description: Query whether shared memory is available to the given reader/writer entity. This gate must be true to use dds_request_loan_of_size. Returns true if shared memory is available, false otherwise.
requirements: entity should be a valid entity handle.
This function is intended to be called before dds_request_loan_of_size to determine availability.

functions.name: dds_request_loan_of_size
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_request_loan_of_size(dds_entity_t writer, size_t size, void **sample);
functions.description: Request/borrow a loaned sample buffer of a specified size from a writer. The loan can later be returned via dds_return_loan or published via dds_write or dds_writedispose (which takes over the loan). Only usable when shared memory is available for the writer (see dds_is_shared_memory_available).
requirements: writer must be a writer entity.
dds_is_shared_memory_available(writer) must be true; otherwise the function must not be used.
sample must be a non-null pointer to receive the borrowed buffer pointer.
size specifies the requested loan size; no explicit range is documented beyond fitting in size_t.
Caller must check return code: DDS_RETCODE_OK on success; DDS_RETCODE_ERROR otherwise as documented.

functions.name: dds_is_loan_available
functions.signature: bool dds_is_loan_available(const dds_entity_t entity);
functions.description: Deprecated. Check whether loaning is available to the given reader/writer. Superseded by dds_request_loan; historically returns whether shared memory is enabled and constraints are met and the type is fixed. The paired loaning function was dds_loan_sample.
requirements: entity should be a valid entity handle.
Only use for legacy code; prefer dds_request_loan and dds_is_shared_memory_available going forward.

functions.name: dds_loan_sample
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_loan_sample(dds_entity_t writer, void **sample);
functions.description: Deprecated. Loan a sample from a writer for publishing with dds_write. Use dds_request_loan instead. May be used only if dds_is_loan_available(writer) is true.
requirements: writer must be a writer entity.
dds_is_loan_available(writer) must be true prior to calling.
sample must be a non-null pointer to receive the loaned sample.
Caller must check return code: DDS_RETCODE_OK if successful, DDS_RETCODE_ERROR otherwise.
Intended to be used with dds_write to publish the loaned sample; otherwise return the loan appropriately.

functions.name: dds_create_statistics
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT struct dds_statistics *dds_create_statistics (dds_entity_t entity);
functions.description: Allocates and populates a new statistics container for the specified DDS entity. Use to obtain a snapshot of available statistics for an entity that supports statistics. Returns NULL if the entity handle is invalid or the entity provides no statistics. The returned structure must be released with dds_delete_statistics when no longer needed.
requirements: entity must refer to a valid DDS entity that supports statistics to obtain a non-NULL result
the returned struct dds_statistics pointer must be freed by calling dds_delete_statistics
do not modify memory owned by the library inside struct dds_statistics (e.g., dds_stat_keyvalue.name)
API is marked unstable; behavior may change between versions

functions.name: dds_refresh_statistics
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_return_t dds_refresh_statistics (struct dds_statistics *stat);
functions.description: Refreshes a previously created statistics structure with current values. Only the timestamp, opaque field, and the values of existing key/value pairs are updated; the set of keys and their types do not change. Use to update a snapshot without reallocating.
requirements: stat must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct dds_statistics previously returned by dds_create_statistics
the referenced entity must still exist; otherwise returns DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER
if the library has been deinitialized, returns DDS_RETCODE_PRECONDITION_NOT_MET
caller must handle return codes: DDS_RETCODE_OK (success), DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER, DDS_RETCODE_PRECONDITION_NOT_MET
do not expect the set of keys or their kinds to change across refreshes

functions.name: dds_delete_statistics
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT void dds_delete_statistics (struct dds_statistics *stat);
functions.description: Frees a statistics object previously created by dds_create_statistics. Passing NULL is a no-op. Succeeds even if the associated entity no longer exists. After deletion, the pointer must not be used.
requirements: stat may be NULL (no operation performed)
each statistics object must be freed at most once
after calling, any pointers into the statistics object (e.g., dds_stat_keyvalue returned by lookup) become invalid and must not be dereferenced

functions.name: dds_lookup_statistic
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT const struct dds_stat_keyvalue *dds_lookup_statistic (const struct dds_statistics *stat, const char *name) ddsrt_nonnull ((2));
functions.description: Looks up a statistic by name within a statistics object and returns a pointer to the matching key/value entry stored inside the object. Returns NULL if stat is NULL or if no key matches name. The returned pointer refers to internal storage and must not be freed or modified.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL pointer (per ddsrt_nonnull((2)) attribute)
stat may be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL
the returned pointer, if non-NULL, points to memory owned by the statistics object and must not be freed or modified
the name must match exactly one of the keys stored in stat to obtain a non-NULL result

functions.name: dds_loaned_sample_ref
functions.signature: DDS_INLINE_EXPORT inline void ddsrt_nonnull_all dds_loaned_sample_ref (dds_loaned_sample_t *loaned_sample)
functions.description: Atomically increments the reference count of a loaned sample. Use when creating an additional reference to a dds_loaned_sample_t that must keep the sample alive across users/threads. The sample is not freed while at least one reference remains.
requirements: loaned_sample must be a non-null pointer (annotated with ddsrt_nonnull_all).
loaned_sample->refc must have been initialized as an atomic reference counter before calling.
loaned_sample must represent a valid, initialized loaned sample object with a correctly set ops.free callback (so paired unref can eventually free it).
May be called from multiple threads; callers must already hold a valid reference when sharing across threads to avoid premature free.

functions.name: dds_loaned_sample_unref
functions.signature: DDS_INLINE_EXPORT inline void ddsrt_nonnull_all dds_loaned_sample_unref (dds_loaned_sample_t *loaned_sample)
functions.description: Atomically decrements the reference count of a loaned sample and, when it reaches 0, calls the implementation-specific free function (ops.free) to release the sample. Use to drop a reference previously obtained (e.g., after use or after a successful store operation that retained a reference).
requirements: loaned_sample must be a non-null pointer (annotated with ddsrt_nonnull_all).
Caller must hold a valid reference prior to calling (the number of unref calls must not exceed the number of ref acquisitions).
loaned_sample->ops.free must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked exactly when the reference count transitions to zero.
Safe for concurrent use; callers must avoid use-after-free by not accessing the sample after their last unref.

functions.name: dds_reader_store_loaned_sample
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_return_t dds_reader_store_loaned_sample (dds_entity_t reader, dds_loaned_sample_t *data) ddsrt_nonnull_all;
functions.description: Constructs serdata of the reader’s type from the provided loaned sample and inserts it into the reader’s history cache. If the constructed serdata references the loan, the function internally increments the loan’s reference count. If the data is not from a known writer, the call is a no-op. Returns a dds_return_t indicating success or the reason for failure.
requirements: reader must refer to a valid, existing reader entity that has not been deleted.
data must be a non-null pointer to a valid dds_loaned_sample_t (annotated with ddsrt_nonnull_all).
The loaned sample’s content and type must be compatible with the reader’s topic type; otherwise the operation may fail (or result in no-op depending on writer recognition).
Caller must check the returned dds_return_t and handle errors (e.g., DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER, DDS_RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION, DDS_RETCODE_ALREADY_DELETED).
If the function retains a reference to the loan (by constructing serdata that references it), the caller must account for the incremented refcount when managing the sample’s lifetime.

Returns a dds_return_t indicating success or the reason for failure.
requirements: reader must refer to a valid, existing reader entity that has not been deleted.
data must be a non-null pointer to a valid dds_loaned_sample_t (annotated with ddsrt_nonnull_all).
ownership_strength must be a valid 32-bit integer representing the writer’s ownership strength expected by the system.

Caller must check and handle the returned dds_return_t, including DDS_RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER, DDS_RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION, and DDS_RETCODE_ALREADY_DELETED.
If the function retains a reference to the loan (by constructing serdata that references it), the caller must account for the incremented refcount when managing the sample’s lifetime.

functions.name: dds_dynamic_type_create
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_dynamic_type_t dds_dynamic_type_create (dds_entity_t entity, dds_dynamic_type_descriptor_t descriptor);
functions.description: Create a new dynamic type from the provided descriptor. The descriptor specifies the kind (primitive/collection/aggregate) and any required attributes (name, bounds, element type, base/aliased type, etc.). Ownership of any referenced types in base_type, element_type, or discriminator_type is transferred to the created type. On return, check the ret field of the returned dds_dynamic_type_t for success before using it.
requirements: entity must be a valid DDS entity (not the pseudo root entity DDS_CYCLONEDDS_HANDLE).
descriptor.kind must be set (required for all types).
descriptor.name is required for structure, union, alias, enum, bitmask, array, and sequence kinds.
For alias kinds, descriptor.base_type must reference the aliased type (required).
For union kinds, descriptor.discriminator_type must be set (required).
For array kinds, descriptor.num_bounds indicates the number of dimensions and descriptor.bounds must supply that many bounds; descriptor.element_type is required.
For sequence kinds, descriptor.num_bounds must be 0 (unbounded) or 1; descriptor.bounds supplies the single bound if present; descriptor.element_type is required.
For map kinds, descriptor.key_element_type applies (if used by implementation).
Ownership of base_type, element_type, and discriminator_type is transferred to the created type and must not be freed or reused by the caller.
Caller must check the returned dds_dynamic_type_t.ret equals DDS_RETCODE_OK before further operations.

The parent type assumes ownership of the member type. For enums/bitmasks, dedicated helpers exist, but the comment notes parent can be enumeration or bitmask as well.

member_descriptor.id may be DDS_DYNAMIC_MEMBER_ID_AUTO (alias DDS_DYNAMIC_MEMBER_ID_INVALID) to auto-assign next available ID; otherwise, a valid member ID has the 4 most significant bits set to 0.
member_descriptor.index controls insertion position; use DDS_DYNAMIC_MEMBER_INDEX_START for first or a value > current max to append (DDS_DYNAMIC_MEMBER_INDEX_END).

For union non-default members, member_descriptor.num_labels must be >= 1 and member_descriptor.labels must point to that many label values; for default members, member_descriptor.default_label must be true and labels/num_labels are not required.
The parent type takes ownership of member_descriptor.type; the caller must not reuse or free it after a successful call.

functions.name: dds_dynamic_type_register
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_return_t dds_dynamic_type_register (dds_dynamic_type_t *type, struct ddsi_typeinfo **type_info);
functions.description: Register (finalize) a dynamic type, making it immutable and storing it in the type library. On success the type’s state becomes RESOLVED and it can no longer be modified. A ddsi_typeinfo handle for the registered type is returned via type_info.
requirements: type must be non-NULL and in the CONSTRUCTING state.
type_info must be non-NULL and writable to receive the ddsi_typeinfo* result.
After successful registration, the type becomes immutable and cannot be modified.

functions.name: dds_dynamic_type_ref
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_dynamic_type_t dds_dynamic_type_ref (dds_dynamic_type_t *type);
functions.description: Increase the reference count of a dynamic type and return a handle to it. Useful when reusing a subtype during construction.
requirements: type must be non-NULL and reference a valid dynamic type.
Caller should treat the returned handle as a referenced instance and must later unref it when no longer needed.

functions.name: dds_dynamic_type_unref
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_return_t dds_dynamic_type_unref (dds_dynamic_type_t *type);
functions.description: Decrease the reference count of a dynamic type; the type is released when the count reaches zero. Documentation in this header lists standard return codes; state-specific details are not fully described here.
requirements: type must be non-NULL and reference a valid dynamic type.
Caller must not use the type after its final unref releases it (exact lifetime semantics beyond standard ref-counting are not specified in this header).

functions.name: dds_dynamic_type_dup
functions.signature: DDS_EXPORT dds_dynamic_type_t dds_dynamic_type_dup (const dds_dynamic_type_t *src);
functions.description: Create a duplicate handle of a dynamic type. The type itself is not deep-copied; dependencies are not duplicated but have their reference counts increased.
requirements: src must be non-NULL and reference a valid dynamic type.
Caller should later unref the duplicate when no longer needed.

functions.name: dds_create_qos_provider
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_create_qos_provider(const char *path, dds_qos_provider_t **provider);
functions.description: Creates and initializes a QoS Provider instance from a supplied system definition, which can be either the textual contents of a system definition or a path to a system definition file. On success, stores the created provider in the output parameter. Intended as the first step before querying QoS profiles. Returns a DDS return code indicating success or failure.
requirements: Available only when DDS_HAS_QOS_PROVIDER is defined at build time.
path must point to a valid, null-terminated C string containing either the system definition text itself or a filesystem path to a system definition file.
provider must be non-null and point to a variable that can receive the resulting dds_qos_provider_t* on success.
Caller must check the returned dds_return_t and proceed only on success.
A successfully created provider must be released with dds_delete_qos_provider to avoid resource leaks.
The provider pointer output remains owned by the QoS Provider implementation; do not free it with general-purpose allocators.

functions.name: dds_create_qos_provider_scope
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_create_qos_provider_scope(const char *path, dds_qos_provider_t **provider, const char *key);
functions.description: Creates and initializes a QoS Provider with an initial scope filter, limiting lookups to QoS entries matching the provided pattern. The key expresses the scope in the format '<library name>::<profile name>::<entity name>'. Returns a DDS return code.
requirements: Available only when DDS_HAS_QOS_PROVIDER is defined at build time.
path must point to a valid, null-terminated C string containing either the system definition text itself or a filesystem path to a system definition file.
provider must be non-null and point to a variable that can receive the resulting dds_qos_provider_t* on success.
key must be a valid, null-terminated C string in the format '<library name>::<profile name>::<entity name>' representing the desired scope/pattern.
Caller must check the returned dds_return_t and proceed only on success.
A successfully created provider must be released with dds_delete_qos_provider to avoid resource leaks.
The provider pointer output remains owned by the QoS Provider implementation; do not free it with general-purpose allocators.

functions.name: dds_qos_provider_get_qos
functions.signature: dds_return_t dds_qos_provider_get_qos(const dds_qos_provider_t *provider, dds_qos_kind_t type, const char *key, const dds_qos_t **qos);
functions.description: Retrieves a QoS object from an existing QoS Provider by specifying the entity kind and a fully-qualified key '<library name>::<profile name>::<entity name>'. On success, returns a pointer to a QoS structure for read-only use. Returns a DDS return code.
requirements: Available only when DDS_HAS_QOS_PROVIDER is defined at build time.
provider must be a valid pointer to a QoS Provider previously created by dds_create_qos_provider or dds_create_qos_provider_scope and not yet deleted.
type must be one of: DDS_PARTICIPANT_QOS, DDS_PUBLISHER_QOS, DDS_SUBSCRIBER_QOS, DDS_TOPIC_QOS, DDS_READER_QOS, or DDS_WRITER_QOS.
key must be a valid, null-terminated C string containing the fully-qualified QoS name in the format '<library name>::<profile name>::<entity name>'.
qos must be non-null and point to a location to receive the resulting const dds_qos_t* on success.
Caller must check the returned dds_return_t and proceed only on success.
The returned QoS pointer is const; the caller must not modify or free it. Its validity is at least tied to the lifetime of the provider (do not use it after the provider is deleted).

functions.name: dds_delete_qos_provider
functions.signature: void dds_delete_qos_provider(dds_qos_provider_t *provider);
functions.description: Finalizes and releases resources held by a QoS Provider instance created by the corresponding create functions. After this call, the provider must not be used.
requirements: Available only when DDS_HAS_QOS_PROVIDER is defined at build time.
provider must be a valid pointer previously returned by a successful create call and not already deleted.
The caller must not use the provider after deletion; any QoS pointers retrieved from the provider become invalid after deletion.
It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure no concurrent operations are in progress on the provider when deleting it (thread-safety not specified).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: provide interesting, valid configuration strings for:
# - dds_create_domain: expects a config string (filenames and/or XML fragments). Empty string is valid.
# - dds_psmx_get_config_option_value: expects a double-\0-terminated list of KEY=VALUE; pairs.
# The fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times. We will return a single bytes buffer that
# concatenates multiple interesting strings separated by NULs so the harness can slice them, or
# provide them as independent FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations depending on the integration.
# To maximize validity:
# 1) Include several plausible CycloneDDS config forms: empty, filename-like, XML snippets,
#    env-URI-like, and malformed-but-still-text. These exercise parsing paths without being junk.
# 2) Include a well-formed PSMX config in double-NUL-terminated form with INSTANCE_NAME and extras.
# 3) Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-./:+=,"


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: str = SAFE_ASCII) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _xml_config(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Minimal valid CycloneDDS XML snippet covering a few knobs
    # Using simple topic/participant configuration bits
    participant_name = _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 12)
    domain_id = str(rng.randint(0, 229))
    entity_name = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10)
    return (
        "<CycloneDDS>"
        "<Domain id=\"" + domain_id + "\">"
        "<General><NetworkInterfaceAddress>auto</NetworkInterfaceAddress>"
        "<AllowMulticast>true</AllowMulticast></General>"
        "<Internal><WriteBatch>true</WriteBatch></Internal>"
        "</Domain>"
        "<Domain id=\"any\">"
        "<Tracing><Verbosity>severe</Verbosity></Tracing>"
        "</Domain>"
        "<Entity><Name>" + entity_name + "</Name></Entity>"
        "<Participants><Participant><Name>" + participant_name + "</Name></Participant></Participants>"
        "</CycloneDDS>"
    )


def _file_uri_config(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Could be used as filename or URI; library treats string as config content or filename
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # filesystem path
        parts = ["/etc/cyclonedds", "conf", _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8) + ".xml"]
        return "/" + "/".join(p.strip("/") for p in parts)
    else:
        # URI form often used via CYCLONEDDS_URI
        scheme = rng.choice(["file://", "env://", "data://"])  # not strictly required but plausible
        tail = _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 15) + ".xml"
        return scheme + tail


def _minimal_xml(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return "<CycloneDDS/>"


def _psmx_double_nul(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build double-\0-terminated config: "KEY=VALUE;\0KEY2=VALUE2;\0\0"
    inst = _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 12)
    # Ensure keys don't contain '=', ';' or NUL
    def clean_key(s: str) -> str:
        return ''.join(ch if ch not in ['=', ';', '\\x00'] else 'A' for ch in s)
    extra_key = clean_key(_rand_ascii(rng, 4, 10))
    extra_val = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 16)
    entries: List[str] = [f"INSTANCE_NAME={inst};", f"{extra_key}={extra_val};"]
    # Occasionally add SERVICE_NAME alias too
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        entries.insert(1, f"SERVICE_NAME={inst};")
    joined = ("\0".join(entries) + "\0\0").encode('utf-8')
    return joined


def _compose_payload(parts: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join parts with a single NUL between logical FUZZ_PARAM_STR chunks to allow consumers to split.
    # Keep inside 4096 bytes.
    out = b"\0".join(parts)
    return out[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings: List[str] = []

    # Include a mix of configuration strings for dds_create_domain
    # 1) Empty (defaults)
    strings.append("")
    # 2) Minimal XML
    strings.append(_minimal_xml(rng))
    # 3) Rich XML config
    strings.append(_xml_config(rng))
    # 4) Filename/URI-like
    strings.append(_file_uri_config(rng))
    # 5) Random ASCII text (still valid as arbitrary text)
    strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 10, 40))

    # Prepare PSMX config as bytes (double-NUL terminated block)
    psmx = _psmx_double_nul(rng)

    # Convert strings to bytes; separate with NUL so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can consume distinct pieces
    parts: List[bytes] = [s.encode('utf-8') for s in strings]
    parts.append(psmx)  # keep the binary block intact; trailing double-NUL preserved

    return _compose_payload(parts)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: topic name (non-empty C string). Used by APIs expecting a DDS Topic name.
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for the topic name and bail on empty.
# Generate interesting, valid UTF-8 strings covering:
# - Common ASCII identifiers
# - Names with namespaces/separators
# - Long names near typical limits
# - Names with spaces and punctuation
# - Unicode (UTF-8) characters
# - Edge cases: leading/trailing spaces, dots, slashes, wildcard-like chars (though allowed as names)
# Resulting bytes must represent a non-empty UTF-8 string (no NUL inside, since C string terminates at NUL).

_MAX_LEN = 512  # keep well below 4096

_ASCII_ID_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
_ASCII_ID_CONT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

# Some predefined interesting names
_PRESET_NAMES: List[str] = [
    "T",
    "Topic",
    "Data",
    "sensor",
    "telemetry",
    "cmd",
    "status",
    "partition/topic",   # slash
    "partition::topic",  # namespace-like
    "ns::mod::Topic42",
    "a.b.c",             # dots
    "topic with spaces",
    "topic-with-dash",
    "topic_with_underscore",
    "topic+plus",
    "topic,comma",
    "topic;semi",
    "topic:colon",
    "topic@at",
    "topic#hash",
    "topic[brackets]",
    "topic{curly}",
    "topic(paren)",
    "topic|pipe",
    "topic~tilde",
    "topic!",
    "topic?",
    "topic=eq",
    "topic^caret",
    "topic$money",
    "topic%percent",
    " leading-space",
    "trailing-space ",
    " surrounding spaces ",
    # Unicode samples
    "Δelta",
    "测量",              # Chinese
    "тема",              # Russian
    "موضوع",             # Arabic
    "トップィック",        # Japanese Katakana-ish
    "emojis-📡-🛰️-✅",
]

def _rand_ascii_identifier(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 1:
        return r.choice(_ASCII_ID_START)
    s = [r.choice(_ASCII_ID_START)]
    s.extend(r.choice(_ASCII_ID_CONT) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return "".join(s)

def _rand_with_separators(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    parts = [
        _rand_ascii_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(3, 10))
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5))
    ]
    sep = r.choice(["::", "/", "."])
    name = sep.join(parts)
    # maybe add suffix/prefix
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        name = (" "+name) if r.random() < 0.5 else (name+" ")
    return name[:max_len] if len(name) > max_len else name

def _rand_unicode_chunk(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Pick from varied unicode ranges
    pools = [
        (0x00A1, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplements (excluding control)
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
        (0x3040, 0x30FF),   # Hiragana/Katakana
        (0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Emojis range part
    ]
    lo, hi = r.choice(pools)
    # Ensure not surrogate range; Python handles fine though
    cp = r.randint(lo, hi)
    return chr(cp)

def _rand_mixed_name(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII words and unicode chunks with symbols
    symbols = "-_ ,.;:@+!?#%[]{}()|~^$="
    chunks = []
    while True:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.45:
            chunks.append(_rand_ascii_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(1, 8)))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            chunks.append(_rand_unicode_chunk(r))
        else:
            chunks.append(r.choice(symbols))
        s = "".join(chunks)
        if len(s.encode('utf-8')) >= max_len:
            break
        if len(chunks) > 3 and r.random() < 0.25:
            break
    # Ensure we don't exceed max_len in bytes
    name = ""
    for ch in chunks:
        if len((name + ch).encode('utf-8')) > max_len:
            break
        name += ch
    # Ensure not empty
    return name if name else "X"

def _long_name(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Create a long but valid name near target_len bytes
    base_parts = []
    while True:
        part = _rand_ascii_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(3, 12))
        sep = r.choice(["::", "/", ".", "_"])
        next_seg = (sep if base_parts else "") + part
        if len(("".join(base_parts) + next_seg).encode('utf-8')) > target_len:
            break
        base_parts.append(next_seg)
        if r.random() < 0.1:
            break
    name = "".join(base_parts)
    return name if name else _rand_ascii_identifier(r, 8, 16)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a strategy
    strategy = r.choices(
        population=["preset", "ascii", "sep", "mixed", "long"],
        weights=[2, 3, 3, 4, 2],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if strategy == "preset":
        name = r.choice(_PRESET_NAMES)
    elif strategy == "ascii":
        name = _rand_ascii_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(1, 32))
    elif strategy == "sep":
        name = _rand_with_separators(r, max_len=min(_MAX_LEN, 128))
    elif strategy == "mixed":
        name = _rand_mixed_name(r, max_len=min(_MAX_LEN, 128))
    else:  # long
        name = _long_name(r, target_len=min(_MAX_LEN, 256))

    # Ensure non-empty and no embedded NULs
    if not name:
        name = "X"
    name = name.replace("\x00", "_")

    # Encode as UTF-8 bytes; caller/fuzzer provides this to FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffer
    data = name.encode('utf-8')
    # Guarantee size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    # Avoid empty after truncation
    if not data:
        data = b"X"
    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target format: opaque binary blob used in multiple places:
# - As keyed sample bytes for dds_lookup_instance / dds_instance_get_key
# - As userdata/topicdata/groupdata/bprop payloads
# We want valid but interesting buffers that resemble typical DDS key payloads and
# small property blobs, with variability while remaining within 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_ALPHA = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
ASCII_DIGITS = b"0123456789"
ASCII_HEX = b"0123456789abcdef"


def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_uuid_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 16-byte GUID-like content
    b = bytearray(_rand(r, 16))
    # Version 4 UUID style tweaks for variety
    b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0F) | 0x40
    b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80
    return bytes(b)


def _make_hex_string(r: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choice(ASCII_HEX) for _ in range(length))


def _make_kv_pairs(r: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Create KEY=VALUE; pairs often seen in properties/config
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        klen = r.randint(3, 10)
        vlen = r.randint(0, 24)
        key = bytes(r.choice(ASCII_ALPHA) for _ in range(klen))
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            # sometimes hex value
            val = _make_hex_string(r, vlen if vlen else r.randint(2, 8))
        else:
            val = _rand(r, vlen)
        parts.append(key + b"=" + val + b";")
    return b"".join(parts)


def _make_cdr_like_header(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal CDR-like header: identifier + options. Not required by API, but helps exercise paths.
    # 2 bytes: identifier (e.g., 0x0002 for XCDR2), 2 bytes: options
    ident = r.choice([0x0000, 0x0001, 0x0002, 0xABCD])
    opts = r.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    return struct.pack(">HH", ident, opts)


def _make_keyed_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a plausible keyed sample:
    # [len topic name][topic][len type name][type][guid(16)][instance_id(8)][key bytes]
    topic = b"Top" + bytes(r.choice(ASCII_ALPHA) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)))
    tname = b"Type" + bytes(r.choice(ASCII_ALPHA) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 12)))
    guid = _make_uuid_like(r)
    instance_id = r.getrandbits(64)
    # key bytes: mix ascii and random
    klen = r.randint(8, 32)
    key = bytes(r.choice(ASCII_ALPHA + ASCII_DIGITS) for _ in range(klen))
    blob = []
    blob.append(struct.pack(">H", len(topic)))
    blob.append(topic)
    blob.append(struct.pack(">H", len(tname)))
    blob.append(tname)
    blob.append(guid)
    blob.append(struct.pack(">Q", instance_id))
    blob.append(struct.pack(">H", len(key)))
    blob.append(key)
    return b"".join(blob)


def _make_userdata_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Either empty, small text, or binary
    mode = r.randrange(4)
    if mode == 0:
        return b""
    elif mode == 1:
        # small ascii message
        n = r.randint(1, 128)
        return bytes(r.choice(ASCII_ALPHA + b" _-./:") for _ in range(n))
    elif mode == 2:
        # kv pairs
        return _make_kv_pairs(r, r.randint(1, 6))
    else:
        n = r.randint(1, 256)
        return _rand(r, n)


def _mix_parts(parts: List[bytes], limit: int) -> bytes:
    out = b""
    for p in parts:
        if len(out) + len(p) > limit:
            break
        out += p
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy: create a bundle-like blob that is still valid as an opaque buffer
    # and is useful across stubs. Start with a small CDR-ish header, then embed
    # a keyed payload, then append property/userdata sections. Keep under MAX_SIZE.

    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # Optional header
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        sections.append(_make_cdr_like_header(r))

    # One or two keyed payloads to improve chance of matching instance lookups
    sections.append(_make_keyed_payload(r))
    if r.random() < 0.35:
        sections.append(_make_keyed_payload(r))

    # Embed a GUID tag section
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        sections.append(b"GUID" + _make_uuid_like(r))

    # Add some kv-style and userdata blobs separated with simple tags
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        sections.append(b"UD\x00" + _make_userdata_blob(r))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        sections.append(b"BP\x00" + _make_kv_pairs(r, r.randint(1, 4)))

    # Maybe append a small random tail
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        sections.append(_rand(r, r.randint(0, 64)))

    data = _mix_parts(sections, MAX_SIZE)

    # Ensure non-empty to satisfy stubs expecting non-empty FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    if not data:
        data = _rand(r, r.randint(1, 64))

    # Bound final size (should already be under limit)
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

import string
from typing import List

# Target: generate buffers that the fuzz stubs will use as FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# Data type: C string (null-terminated in C; here we provide bytes with a trailing NUL)
# Strategy:
# - Produce a small catalog of interesting ASCII strings that exercise the QoS/property APIs:
#   * Keys for properties and partitions (alnum/underscore, varying lengths)
#   * Values containing typical characters but avoiding embedded NUL or dangerous size
#   * Partition lists encoded as multiple NUL-terminated strings in one buffer separated by '\n' for the fuzzer to split
# - Also include strings that look like double-\0-terminated PSMX config blobs
# - Include a plausible filesystem path for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# - Constrain total size <= 4096 bytes

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:. /"
SAFE_KEY = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
SAFE_PART = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:/.*?"


def _rand_str(rng: random.Random, alphabet: str, lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(lo, hi)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 and append NUL for C string compatibility
    return s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"


def _make_property_entry(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # name and value suitable for dds_qset_prop*_ family
    name = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_KEY, 1, 16)
    # Values can be longer
    val = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 0, 64)
    return [_cstr(name), _cstr(val)]


def _make_partition_list(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Up to 4 partition names, some empty allowed
    n = rng.randint(0, 4)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(n):
        # small partitions to match stub caps
        parts.append(_cstr(_rand_str(rng, SAFE_PART, 0, 24)))
    if n == 0:
        # also add a single empty C-string to exercise n==0 with NULL vs non-NULL scenarios elsewhere
        parts.append(_cstr(""))
    return parts


def _make_binary_blob(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # name plus a small binary-like ascii payload (since we only return C strings, keep texty)
    name = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_KEY, 1, 16)
    payload = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 0, 128)
    return [_cstr(name), _cstr(payload)]


def _make_psmx_double_nul_conf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build: KEY=VALUE;\0KEY2=VALUE2;\0\0
    def clean_key(s: str) -> str:
        s = ''.join(c if c in SAFE_KEY else 'A' for c in s)
        return s or 'X'
    inst = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 1, 24)
    k2 = clean_key(_rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 1, 12))
    v2 = _rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 0, 24)
    conf = f"INSTANCE_NAME={inst};\x00{k2}={v2};\x00\x00"
    return conf.encode('utf-8')


def _make_qos_provider_key(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # '<library>::<profile>::<entity>' as C string
    comp = lambda: _rand_str(rng, SAFE_KEY, 1, 16)
    key = f"{comp()}::{comp()}::{comp()}"
    return _cstr(key)


def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide a reasonable path-like filename string
    # The harness will map FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to a temp file path containing fuzz data, but we supply a plausible path
    base = _rand_str(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, 5, 12)
    ext = rng.choice([".xml", ".conf", ".txt", ""])
    path = rng.choice([f"/tmp/{base}{ext}", f"C:/temp/{base}{ext}", f"./{base}{ext}"])
    return _cstr(path)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Filename for provider constructors
    chunks.append(_make_filename(rng))

    # 2) Several property name/value pairs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.extend(_make_property_entry(rng))

    # 3) Partition lists (as individual C strings; fuzzer consumes per-call)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.extend(_make_partition_list(rng))

    # 4) Binary property name + payload (textual payload OK for setters; sz controls binary)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        chunks.extend(_make_binary_blob(rng))

    # 5) QoS Provider scope keys
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        chunks.append(_make_qos_provider_key(rng))

    # 6) PSMX double-NUL config blob (not a single C string; keep as-is)
    chunks.append(_make_psmx_double_nul_conf(rng))

    # 7) A few generic small strings to be used where arbitrary names are needed
    for _ in range(3):
        chunks.append(_cstr(_rand_str(rng, SAFE_ASCII, 0, 24)))

    # Concatenate with a separator that is safe to parse: we simply pack back-to-back C strings/blobs
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    # Enforce size cap
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

# Fuzzer behavior:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() is used to supply the name; stub truncates to 64 bytes and ensures non-empty by replacing empty with "x".
# - Therefore, providing a valid, non-empty, printable C string of length up to 64 will exercise normal paths.
# - Interesting cases include: min length (1), max length (64), mixed characters, spaces, punctuation, and multi-byte UTF-8.
# - The generator returns bytes; the fuzzer will use it as the backing buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

PRINTABLE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:/@+[]{}()#%&!$^~"  # safe printable set

UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "ΔDDS",            # Greek
    "名称",             # CJK
    "пример",          # Cyrillic
    "नाम",             # Devanagari
    "नाम🚀",           # Emoji
]

def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def _choose_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose among several shape categories to cover different paths
    choice = rng.randrange(8)
    if choice == 0:
        # Minimal non-empty
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Short readable token
        L = rng.randint(2, 12)
        return _rand_printable(rng, L)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Include spaces and punctuation
        L = rng.randint(8, 24)
        s = _rand_printable(rng, L)
        return s.strip() or s  # keep as-is; fuzzer only requires non-empty
    elif choice == 3:
        # Max length 64 ASCII
        return _rand_printable(rng, 64)
    elif choice == 4:
        # Prefix + numeric suffix pattern
        prefix = rng.choice(["participant", "publisher", "subscriber", "reader", "writer"]) 
        num = rng.randint(0, 99999)
        base = f"{prefix}-{num}"
        # Ensure <= 64, possibly extend with random chars
        if len(base) < 64:
            extra = _rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 64 - len(base)))
            base += extra
        return base[:64]
    elif choice == 5:
        # UTF-8 sample possibly combined with ASCII
        base = rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
        tail_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, 60 - len(base)))
        return (base + _rand_printable(rng, tail_len))[:64]
    elif choice == 6:
        # Repeated pattern to test truncation boundaries
        token = rng.choice(["A", "ab", "xyz", "Qos"]) 
        reps = max(1, 64 // max(1, len(token)) + rng.randint(-1, 1))
        s = (token * reps)[:64]
        return s if s else "x"
    else:
        # Mixed case with separators
        parts: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            parts.append(_rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(1, 10)))
        s = '/'.join(parts)
        return s[:64] or "x"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    name = _choose_name(rng)
    # Ensure not empty and avoid embedded NULs; Python strings won't contain NULs unless explicitly added
    if not name:
        name = "x"
    # Return as bytes without a manual NUL terminator; the fuzzer/framework will treat this as a C string buffer
    # Keep total size <= 4096
    b = name.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
